weakest_inference: The claim in Part 2 that 'the process cannot get stuck for p before its valuations reduce to the invariant gcd' informally argues per-prime progress under adversarial global move choices, but this per-prime progress argument is not logically required—the proof instead correctly relies on global termination (Part 1) forcing K=1, which simultaneously forces at most one positive p-valuation for all primes.
counterexample_search: No counterexample found; invariant holds in all tested cases
summary: The proof is fully correct and rigorous. Part 1 establishes termination via the well-founded lexicographic measure (K, ΣΩ) where K=count>1 and S=sum of prime factor counts. Every move strictly decreases (K,S), forcing termination with K≤1; since the product never increases from its initial value >1, K=1 exactly. Part 2 proves uniqueness via the invariant that for each prime p, the gcd of the multiset of p-adic valuations is preserved by the move (a,b)→(min(a,b),|a-b|), a Euclidean step. At termination K=1 implies the final multiset for p is {v_p(M),0,…,0} whose gcd is v_p(M), so v_p(M) equals the initial gcd. The final M=∏p p^{gcd_i v_p(a_i)} is uniquely determined by the initial multiset. No circular dependencies, no gaps, no required fixes. The informal per-prime progress remark in Part 2 is expositionally weak but logically superfluous.
